<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Except as disclosed herein, there have been no material changes in ArcelorMittal&#146;s
consolidated capitalization and indebtedness since September&nbsp;30, 2022. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Between October&nbsp;1, 2022 and November&nbsp;14, 2022,
ArcelorMittal has repurchased 11,776,546 shares at a cost of &#128;257,713,521.51 (equivalent to USD 252,855,380.11). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of
September&nbsp;30, 2022, ArcelorMittal had $0.9&nbsp;billion of consolidated secured indebtedness outstanding. As of September&nbsp;30, 2022, ArcelorMittal had $5.5&nbsp;billion of indebtedness available to be drawn under a revolving credit
facility, all of which would be unsecured and ArcelorMittal South Africa had a ZAR 3.5&nbsp;billion borrowing base facility, under which ZAR 1.5&nbsp;billion ($83 million) had been drawn, all of which is or would be secured. On July&nbsp;27, 2022,
the Company entered into a $2.2&nbsp;billion bridge term facility agreement with a financial institution. The facility may be applied toward the purchase price for the intended acquisition of Companhia Sider&uacute;rgica do Pec&eacute;m, as well as
the refinancing of its existing indebtedness and the payment of related fees, costs and expenses. As of June&nbsp;30, 2022, ArcelorMittal had guaranteed $4.4&nbsp;billion of debt of its associates and joint ventures. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">2 </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="right">Exhibit 99.2 </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>ArcelorMittal reports third quarter 2022 results </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>On November</B><B></B><B>&nbsp;10, 2022 </B>- ArcelorMittal (referred to as &#147;ArcelorMittal&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) (MT (New York, Amsterdam, Paris,
Luxembourg), MTS (Madrid)), the world&#146;s leading integrated steel and mining company, announced results<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">1,2 </SUP>for the three-month (&#147;3Q&#148;) and nine-month (&#147;9M&#148;) periods ended
September&nbsp;30, 2022. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:20pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Key highlights: </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Health and safety performance: </B>Protecting the health and well-being of employees remains the Company&#146;s
overarching priority; LTIF rate<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</SUP> of 0.54x in 3Q 2022 as compared to 0.67x in 2Q 2022 </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Steel spread compression and seasonally lower shipments</B>: 3Q 2022 was impacted by a negative price-cost effect,
energy costs headwinds and a 5.6% sequential decrease in steel shipments to 13.6 Mt <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-7.1%</FONT> lower vs. 3Q 2021). Steel shipments remain broadly stable <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-on-year</FONT></FONT> excluding ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih which is impacted by the ongoing war in Ukraine </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Operating income:</B> $1.7&nbsp;billion in 3Q 2022 (vs. $4.5&nbsp;billion in 2Q 2022); 9M 2022 operating income of
$10.6&nbsp;billion (vs. $12.4&nbsp;billion in 9M 2021) </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Net income:</B> $1.0&nbsp;billion in 3Q 2022 (vs. $3.9&nbsp;billion in 2Q 2022); 9M 2022 net income of $9.0&nbsp;billion
(vs. $10.9&nbsp;billion net income in 9M 2021) </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Share repurchases driving enhanced value:</B> Company repurchased a further 31&nbsp;million shares during the quarter
(96.2&nbsp;million in 9M 2022); diluted share count 873&nbsp;million at end of September&nbsp;30, 2022 (vs. 1,224&nbsp;million at end of September&nbsp;30, 2020<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">18</SUP>); 3Q 2022 basic EPS of
$1.11/share; 9M 2022 basic EPS of $9.76/share vs $9.52/share for 9M 2021 benefiting from lower share count </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Further cash generation: </B>$2.0&nbsp;billion net cash provided by operating activities; capital expenditures of
$0.8&nbsp;billion, dividends paid to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> shareholders of $0.1 billion), working capital release expected in 4Q 2022 </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Financial strength:</B> Long-term debt and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">short-term</FONT> debt (&#147;gross
debt&#148;) of $9.0&nbsp;billion at the end of September 2022, compared to gross debt of $8.8&nbsp;billion and $8.4&nbsp;billion as of June&nbsp;30, 2022 and December&nbsp;31, 2021, respectively; cash and cash equivalents of $5.1&nbsp;billion as of
September&nbsp;30, 2022, compared to $4.6&nbsp;billion and $4.4&nbsp;billion as of June&nbsp;30, 2022 and December&nbsp;31, 2021, respectively; long-term debt and short-term debt less cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash and other
restricted funds (&#147;net debt&#148;) of $4.0&nbsp;billion as of September&nbsp;30, 2022, compared to $4.2&nbsp;billion and $4.0&nbsp;billion as of June&nbsp;30, 2022 and December&nbsp;31, 2021, respectively. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:20pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Strategic update: </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Decarbonization leadership: </B>ArcelorMittal breaks ground on first transformational
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">low-carbon</FONT> emissions steelmaking project in Dofasco (Canada)<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">17</SUP> </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt"><B>Strategic growth: </B>AMNS India announced its strategy to capture growth, expand its market share and play a leading
role in the development of the Indian steel industry. Expansion of the Hazira plant to a ~15Mt capacity by early 2026 is underway including automotive downstream and enhancements to iron ore operations, with capital expenditures of approximately
$7.4&nbsp;billion </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
</DIV></Center>

~31&nbsp;million shares or ~$0.7bn) of the previously announced share <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">buy-back</FONT> program which totaled 60&nbsp;million shares, with the balance to be completed by the end of May 2023 </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

</TABLE></DIV> <P STYLE="margin-top:24pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Commenting, Aditya Mittal, ArcelorMittal Chief Executive Officer, said: </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">&#147;The strong market conditions enjoyed for much of the past two years deteriorated in the third quarter as seasonally lower shipments, a reduction in exceptional
price levels, destocking and higher energy costs combined to put profits under pressure. The business responded quickly to the changing environment, cutting higher cost capacity to manage addressable demand and reduce fixed costs, and reducing
European gas consumption by 30%. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The group&#146;s decarbonization goals remain a central part of the strategy, with a key development being the ground breaking last
month in Ontario, Canada, for a new <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">DRI-EAF</FONT> plant, which is hydrogen ready. This is an important milestone in our decarbonization roadmap and has been achieved thanks to support from both the regional and
federal governments. With COP27 underway we hope for progress on measures that can accelerate the road to net zero, including the scaling up of renewable energy, critical for both the decarbonization of steel and enhanced energy security. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The short-term outlook for the industry remains uncertain and caution is appropriate. But, ArcelorMittal has the strength, resilience and experience to face the future
with confidence. Supported by a strong balance sheet, we will continue to focus on executing our strategy, designed to ensure our long-term sector leadership, as well as deliver sustainable investor returns.&#148; </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">Page 2 </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Sustainable development and safety performance </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Health and safety - Own personnel and contractors lost time injury frequency rate</B><SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top"></SUP><FONT
STYLE="font-family:ARIAL; font-size:6.5pt"><SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">16<B></B></SUP><B> </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:30pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Protecting the health and wellbeing of
employees is the Company&#146;s overarching priority with ongoing strict adherence to World Health Organization guidelines (in respect of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19),</FONT> and specific government guidelines have been followed and
implemented. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Health and safety performance based on own personnel and contractors lost time injury frequency (&#147;LTIF&#148;) rate was 0.54x in the third quarter
of 2022 (&#147;3Q 2022&#148;) as compared to 0.67x in the second quarter of 2022 (&#147;2Q 2022) and 0.76x in the third quarter of 2021<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</SUP> (&#147;3Q 2021&#148;). Health and safety performance in the
first nine months of 2022 (&#147;9M 2022&#148;) was 0.63x as compared to 0.80x in the first nine months of 2021 (&#147;9M 2021&#148;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Own personnel and

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Sustainable development highlights &#150; leading the decarbonization of the steel industry: </B></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">On November&nbsp;3, 2022, ArcelorMittal announced it has invested $25&nbsp;million in nuclear innovation company TerraPower
through its XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&reg;</SUP> innovation fund<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">8</SUP>. The investment is part of an $830&nbsp;million equity raise TerraPower has concluded, which is the
largest private raise among advanced nuclear companies. TerraPower, which was founded by Bill Gates in 2008, entered the nuclear energy arena because the company&#146;s founders saw clean energy as the pathway to lift billions out of poverty. It has
spent the last decade investing in and developing ground-breaking nuclear technologies. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Its flagship technology is Natrium<SUP
STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP>, which features a cost-competitive sodium fast reactor combined with a molten salt energy storage system. This combination will provide clean, flexible energy and integrate seamlessly into power
grids with high penetrations of renewables. TerraPower is experiencing significant growth, and is currently building its first Natrium<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> reactor, a TerraPower and GE Hitachi technology, as
part of the U.S. Department of Energy&#146;s Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP). The facility, being constructed near the site of a retiring coal plant in Kemmerer, Wyoming, will feature a 345 MWe sodium fast reactor alongside an energy
storage system that can boost output to 500 MWe during peak demand. Large scale, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">first-of-a-kind,</FONT></FONT></FONT> energy generation projects like
the Natrium<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> project take years to come to fruition, and TerraPower is targeting an <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-service</FONT> date for the project within this decade. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">On October&nbsp;13, 2022, ArcelorMittal together with the governments of Canada and Ontario, broke ground on its
CAD$1.8&nbsp;billion investment decarbonization project at the ArcelorMittal Dofasco plant in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. The governments of Canada and Ontario having committed CAD$400&nbsp;million and CAD$500&nbsp;million respectively to the overall
project cost. The project will fundamentally change the way steel is made at ArcelorMittal Dofasco, transitioning the site to direct reduced iron-electric arc furnace steelmaking, which carries a considerably lower carbon footprint and removes coal
from the ironmaking process. The new 2.5Mt capacity DRI furnace will initially operate on natural gas but will be constructed &#145;hydrogen ready&#146; so it can transition to green hydrogen when a sufficient and cost-effective supply becomes
available.<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">17</SUP> </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">On October&nbsp;4, 2022, ArcelorMittal announced it has invested a further $17.5&nbsp;million in Form Energy Inc. via its
XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&reg;</SUP> innovation fund. This is the second investment ArcelorMittal has made in the company, following its initial investment of $25&nbsp;million announced in July 2021. Form Energy is
developing, manufacturing, and commercializing a new class of cost-effective, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">multi-day</FONT> energy storage systems that will enable a reliable and fully renewable electric grid year-round. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">On September&nbsp;22, 2022, ArcelorMittal announced that ArcelorMittal Poland had received ResponsibleSteel<SUP
STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> certification, following a successful audit carried out by DNV Poland which confirmed that the business fulfils the criteria required to earn certification against the ResponsibleSteel Standard.
ArcelorMittal Poland is the first cluster of sites to be certified in Eastern Europe by ResponsibleSteel, the industry&#146;s first global multi-stakeholder standard and certification initiative. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">Page 3 </P>

<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Analysis of results for 3Q 2022 versus 2Q 2022 and 3Q 2021 </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Total steel shipments in 3Q 2022 were 13.6Mt, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-5.6%</FONT> lower as compared with 14.4Mt in 2Q 2022, largely reflecting weaker demand and
seasonality in Europe <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-11.1%),</FONT> Brazil <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-5.5%)</FONT> mainly due to lower exports, NAFTA <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-4.6%)</FONT> offset in part by higher shipments in
ACIS +37.6%. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">3Q 2022 steel shipments were <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-7.1%</FONT> lower as compared with 14.6Mt in 3Q 2021, largely reflecting weaker demand
in Europe <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-6.2%)</FONT> and the war in Ukraine <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-29.2%)</FONT> offset in part by NAFTA (+2.6%). Excluding the impact of Ukraine, steel shipments in 3Q 2022 declined by <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-1.0%</FONT> as compared to 3Q 2021 with declines in Europe <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-6.3%,</FONT> offset by ACIS +17.0%, NAFTA +2.5% and Brazil +0.3%. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Sales in 3Q 2022 were $19.0&nbsp;billion as compared to $22.1&nbsp;billion for 2Q 2022 and $20.2&nbsp;billion for 3Q 2021. As compared to 2Q 2022, the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-14.3%</FONT> decrease in sales was primarily due to lower average steel selling prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-11.3%),</FONT> lower steel shipment volumes and lower iron ore reference prices <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-24.8%).</FONT> Sales in 3Q 2022 were <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-6.2%</FONT> lower as compared to 3Q 2021 primarily due to lower steel shipments <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-7.1%)</FONT> and lower iron ore
reference prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-36.5%).</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Depreciation for 3Q 2022 was $628&nbsp;million as compared to $669&nbsp;million for 2Q 2022 and
$590&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. Depreciation was lower in 3Q 2022 than 2Q 2022 primarily due to foreign exchange impacts. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Operating income for 3Q 2022 was
$1.7&nbsp;billion as compared to $4.5&nbsp;billion in 2Q 2022 and $5.3&nbsp;billion for 3Q 2021, reflecting negative price-cost effects, lower volumes, higher energy costs and impacted in 3Q 2022 by $0.5&nbsp;billion of <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</FONT> inventory related charges to reflect the net realizable value of inventory under IFRS with declining market prices in Europe and partially offset by a $0.1&nbsp;billion purchase gain on the acquisition of a
Hot Briquetted Iron (&#145;HBI&#146;) plant in Texas, and in 3Q 2021 by $123&nbsp;million related to expected costs for the decommissioning of the dam at the Serra Azul mine in Brazil. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Income from associates, joint ventures and other investments<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">9</SUP> for 3Q 2022 was $59&nbsp;million as compared to
$578&nbsp;million for 2Q 2022 and $778&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. 3Q 2022 includes lower contribution from AMNS Calvert<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">5</SUP> impacted by a negative price-cost effect and with lagged cost of slab
inventory that does not reflect prevailing slab market prices, AMNS India<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">4</SUP> (negative price-cost effects) and European investees impacted by negative price-cost effects. 2Q 2022 income from
associates, joint ventures and other investments included $0.1&nbsp;billion income for Acciaierie d&#146;Italia arising from recognition of a deferred tax asset. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Net interest expense (interest expense less interest income) in 3Q 2022 was $37&nbsp;million as compared to $53&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and lower than $62&nbsp;million
in 3Q 2021, reflecting higher gains from interest income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Foreign exchange and other net financing losses (revaluation of financial instruments, net foreign
exchange income/expense (i.e., the net effects of transactions in a foreign currency other than the functional currency of a subsidiary) and other net financing costs (which mainly include bank fees, accretion of defined benefit and long-term
liabilities, revaluation of derivative instruments and other charges that cannot be directly linked to operating results)) in 3Q 2022 were $247&nbsp;million as compared to losses of $183&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and $339&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. 3Q
2022 includes foreign exchange loss of $108&nbsp;million compared to $152&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and a gain of $22&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">ArcelorMittal recorded
an income tax expense of $371&nbsp;million (including deferred tax benefit of $23 million) in 3Q 2022, lower as compared to an income tax expense of $826&nbsp;million (including deferred tax benefit of $74 million) in 2Q 2022 due to lower taxable
results. Income tax expense in 3Q 2021 was $882&nbsp;million (including deferred tax benefit of $56 million). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">ArcelorMittal recorded a net income attributable to
equity holders of the parent for 3Q 2022 of $993&nbsp;million as compared to $3,923&nbsp;million for 2Q 2022, and $4,621&nbsp;million for 3Q 2021. ArcelorMittal&#146;s basic earnings per common share for 3Q 2022 was lower at $1.11 as compared to
$4.25 in 2Q 2022 and $4.17 in 3Q 2021. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">Page 4 </P>

</DIV></Center>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">* NAFTA steel shipments include shipments sourced by NAFTA from Group subsidiaries and sold to the Calvert JV that are eliminated on
consolidation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">NAFTA segment crude steel production increased by +4.1% to 2.1Mt in 3Q 2022, as compared to 2.0Mt in 2Q 2022 (which had been negatively impacted by
labour actions in Mexico and maintenance in Canada). Crude steel production in 3Q 2022 increased by +6.6% as compared to 3Q 2021 which had been impacted by operational disruptions (including the impact of hurricane Ida) in Mexico. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Steel shipments in 3Q 2022 decreased <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-4.6%</FONT> to 2.3Mt, as compared to 2.5Mt in 2Q 2022 due to weaker demand, and increased by +2.6%
as compared to 3Q 2021 which had been impacted by the factors discussed above. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Sales in 3Q 2022 decreased by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-5.9%</FONT> to
$3.4&nbsp;billion, as compared to $3.7&nbsp;billion in 2Q 2022 primarily on account of lower average steel selling prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-9.6%)</FONT> and lower steel shipment volumes, partly offset by the scope effect of
ArcelorMittal Texas HBI (consolidated as from June&nbsp;30, 2022). Sales were stable in 3Q 2022 as compared to 3Q 2021 at $3.4&nbsp;billion primarily on account of lower average steel selling prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-8.6%)</FONT>
offset by higher steel shipment volumes (+2.6%) and the scope effect of ArcelorMittal Texas HBI. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Operating income in 3Q 2022 declined
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-24.5%</FONT> to $616&nbsp;million as compared to $817&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-33.4%</FONT> lower as compared to $925&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. Operating income for 3Q 2022
included $0.1&nbsp;billion from the purchase gain on the acquisition of the HBI plant in Texas. Operating income in 3Q 2022 was lower compared to 2Q 2022, primarily due to a negative price-cost effect and the impact of lower steel shipments. The
newly acquired HBI plant in Texas contributed $10&nbsp;million in operating income during 3Q 2022. 2Q 2022 was impacted negatively by $0.1&nbsp;billion from labor action in Mexico. Operating income in 3Q 2022 was lower as compared to 3Q 2021 mainly
due to a negative price-cost effect. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:14pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Brazil<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">14</SUP> </B></P>

in 2Q 2022 and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-4.6%</FONT> as compared to 3Q 2021. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Steel shipments of 2.8Mt in 3Q 2022 were
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-5.5%</FONT> lower as compared to 3.0Mt at 2Q 2022, primarily due to lower exports, but stable as compared to 3Q 2021. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Sales in 3Q
2022 decreased by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-12.5%</FONT> to $3.5&nbsp;billion as compared to $4.0&nbsp;billion in 2Q 2022, primarily due to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-7.8%</FONT> decrease in average steel selling prices. Sales in 3Q
2022 were <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-3.3%</FONT> lower than $3.6&nbsp;billion at 3Q 2021 primarily on account of lower average steel selling prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-4.9%).</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Operating income in 3Q 2022 of $598&nbsp;million was lower as compared to $1,201&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and $1,164&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. Operating income in 3Q 2021
was impacted by charges of $123&nbsp;million related to expected costs for the decommissioning of the dam at the Serra Azul mine in Brazil. Operating income in 3Q 2022 decreased by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-50.2%</FONT> compared to 2Q 2022,
primarily </P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Europe segment crude steel production declined by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-3.2%</FONT> to 8.0Mt in 3Q 2022 as compared to 8.3Mt
in 2Q 2022. Production was <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-12.0%</FONT> lower as compared to 9.1Mt in 3Q 2021 given significantly lower apparent demand and curtailed production in light of higher energy prices. Given the weaker macroeconomic
conditions and order book, high energy and carbon costs and rising imports, the Company announced further, more significant, production curtailments commencing in 4Q 2022 (in France, Spain, Germany and Poland)<SUP
STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">19</SUP> to bring supply in line with addressable demand. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Steel shipments declined by
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-11.1%</FONT> to 7.1Mt in 3Q 2022 as compared to 8.0Mt in 2Q 2022 due to seasonality and lower demand. Shipments declined by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-6.2%</FONT> as compared to 7.6Mt in 3Q 2021 primarily due
to weaker apparent demand. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Sales in 3Q 2022 decreased by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-20.5%</FONT> to $10.7&nbsp;billion, as compared to $13.4&nbsp;billion in
2Q 2022, due to a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-11.1%</FONT> reduction in steel shipments and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-11.0%</FONT> lower average selling prices (including a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-5.5%</FONT> negative forex
translation impact). Sales declined by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-4.8%</FONT> as compared to 3Q 2021 primarily due to lower steel shipments offset in part by higher average steel selling prices (+4.7%). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Operating income in 3Q 2022 significantly declined to $158&nbsp;million as compared to $2,063&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and lower than $1,925&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021.
Operating income in 3Q 2022 was impacted by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</FONT> inventory charges of $473&nbsp;million, reflecting the net realizable value of inventory under IFRS with declining market prices. Operating income in 3Q
2022 declined significantly compared to 2Q 2022, due to the impacts of lower steel shipments, negative price-cost effect, higher energy costs (approximately $0.3&nbsp;billion higher compared to 2Q 2022, with higher market prices partially offset by
hedges in place) and negative forex translation impact ($0.1 billion). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:60pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>ACIS<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">13</SUP> </B></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">ACIS segment crude steel production in 3Q 2022 was +46.0% higher at 1.8Mt as compared to 1.3Mt in 2Q 2022 primarily due to the recovery
in South Africa following the impact from a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2-week</FONT> labour action and logistic issues in the prior quarter. Crude steel production in 3Q 2022 was <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-38.9%</FONT> below 3.0Mt in 3Q
2021 primarily due to lower steel production in Ukraine due to the ongoing war. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">Page 6 </P>

</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always">
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">One of the three blast furnaces in Ukraine, blast furnace No.6 which is approximately 20% of Kryvyi Rih capacity, was
restarted on April&nbsp;11, 2022. During 3Q 2022, iron ore production was temporarily suspended due to weaker demand and logistic constraints (versus ~55% capacity rate in 2Q 2022) and has restarted in early October 2022 at ~25% level. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Steel shipments in 3Q 2022 increased by +37.6% to 1.7Mt as compared to 1.2Mt in 2Q 2022 primarily due to higher exports from Kazakhstan. Shipments were <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-29.2%</FONT> lower as compared to 2.4Mt in 3Q 2021, primarily in Ukraine due the ongoing war. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Sales in 3Q 2022 increased by +5.7% to
$1.6&nbsp;billion as compared to $1.5&nbsp;billion in 2Q 2022, primarily due to higher steel shipments, offset in part by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-16.5%</FONT> lower average steel selling prices. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Operating loss in 3Q 2022 of $55&nbsp;million compared to an operating income of $43&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and $808&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. Operating loss in 3Q 2022
reflected a decline compared to 2Q 2022, primarily due to lower average steel selling prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-16.5%)</FONT> offset in part by higher steel shipments. 2Q 2022 had also been impacted by higher costs including labour
action and logistic issues in ArcelorMittal South Africa ($0.1 billion). Operating loss in 3Q 2022 reflected a significant decline compared to 3Q 2021 due to lower steel shipments <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-29.2%)</FONT> and lower average
steel selling prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-10.5%).</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Mining </B></P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">Note: Mining segment comprises iron ore operations of ArcelorMittal Mines Canada and ArcelorMittal Liberia. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Iron ore production decreased in 3Q 2022 by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-5.3%</FONT> to 6.9Mt as compared to 7.3Mt in 2Q 2022, but marginally higher than 6.8Mt in
3Q 2021. Lower production in 3Q 2022 as compared to 2Q 2022 was primarily due to lower production in AMMC<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">6</SUP> mainly due to impacts of exceptionally heavy rains in September 2022. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Iron ore shipments decreased in 3Q 2022 by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-8.4%</FONT> to 6.9Mt as compared to 7.5Mt in 2Q 2022, primarily driven by the impact of
lower production on shipments at AMMC. 3Q 2022 iron ore shipments were stable as compared to 3Q 2021. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Operating income in 3Q 2022 was $254&nbsp;million as compared
to $463&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and $741&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. Operating income in 3Q 2022 decreased <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-45.1%</FONT> as compared to 2Q 2022, largely reflecting the effect of lower iron ore reference prices <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-24.8%),</FONT> lower quality premia and lower shipments <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-8.4%),</FONT> offset in part by lower freight costs. Operating income in 3Q 2022 was
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-65.7%</FONT> lower as compared to 3Q 2021, primarily due to lower iron ore reference prices <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(-36.5%)</FONT> and lower quality premia. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Joint ventures </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">ArcelorMittal has investments in
various joint ventures and associate entities globally. The Company considers the Calvert (50% equity interest) and AMNS India (60% equity interest) joint ventures to be of particular strategic importance, warranting more detailed disclosures to
improve the understanding of their operational performance and value to the Company. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Calvert<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">5</SUP> </B></P>

third parties, including stainless steel slabs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL">** Shipments: including shipments of finished products processed on a hire work basis for ArcelorMittal group
entities and third parties, including stainless steel products. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Calvert&#146;s hot strip mill (&#147;HSM&#148;) production during 3Q 2022 decreased by <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-6.4%</FONT> to 1.1Mt, as compared to 2Q 2022 and by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-14.9%</FONT> as compared to 1.2Mt in 3Q 2021. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Steel shipments in 3Q 2022 were <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-8.3%</FONT> below 2Q 2022 due to weaker demand. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Calvert&#146;s results during 3Q 2022 were significantly lower than in 2Q 2022 primarily due to negative price-cost effect resulting from the decline in sales prices for
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-contract</FONT> volumes while cost continues to be impacted by the lagged cost of slabs and inventory that does not reflect the prevailing market prices. </P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Crude steel production in 3Q 2022 was stable at 1.7Mt as compared to 2Q 2022 but <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-12.1%</FONT> lower as
compared to 1.9Mt in 3Q 2021 on account of maintenance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Steel shipments in 3Q 2022 increased by +8.2% to 1.6Mt as compared to 1.5Mt in 2Q 2022 but lower as compared
to 1.8Mt in 3Q 2021. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">AMNS India&#146;s results during 3Q 2022 were lower compared to 2Q 2022, due to lower selling prices, higher coal costs and lower pellet sales
contribution (following the introduction of the export duty during the prior quarter) offset in part by higher steel shipments. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">Page 8 </P>

</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always">
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Liquidity and Capital Resources </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Net cash provided by operating activities for 3Q 2022 was $1,981&nbsp;million as compared to $2,554&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and $2,442&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. Net cash
provided by operating activities in 3Q 2022 includes a working capital investment of $580&nbsp;million including an outflow of $2,472&nbsp;million for trade payables partly offset by inflows of $916&nbsp;million and $976&nbsp;million for inventories
and trade accounts receivable, respectively, as compared to investments of $1,008&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 including an outflow of $2,481&nbsp;million for inventories partly offset by inflows of $169&nbsp;million and $1,304&nbsp;million for trade
accounts receivable and trade payables, respectively, and $2,896&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021 including outflows of $3,167&nbsp;million and $187&nbsp;million for inventories and trade accounts receivable, respectively, partly offset by an inflow of
$458&nbsp;million for trade payables. 3Q 2022 working capital requirements were driven primarily by the lagged effects of higher raw material costs and higher energy costs on steel inventories. Based on current market conditions, the Company expects
a working capital release in 4Q 2022. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Capital expenditures in 3Q 2022 amounted to $784&nbsp;million compared with $655&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and $675&nbsp;million
in 3Q 2021. Full year 2022 capital expenditures guidance has been reduced to $3.5&nbsp;billion (from $4.2&nbsp;billion previous guidance) implying 4Q 2022 capital expenditures of ~$1.5&nbsp;billion. The reduction in capital expenditures guidance
reflects some moderate delays to certain strategic and decarbonization spending plans due to project mobilization/contractors but these are now accelerating. There has also been a $0.2&nbsp;billion reduction from foreign exchange effects relative to
initial 2022 budget. Sustaining capital expenditures are expected to increase in 4Q 2022 (although the full year 2022 amount is lower than previous guidance) as the Company capitalizes on a period of lower production and prepares for anticipated
future stronger apparent demand. Full year 2023 capital expenditure plans and guidance will be provided at full year 2022 results in February 2023, but second half 2022 run rate levels are a good base-line for full year 2023. Given the previously
announced strategic pipeline ($3.65&nbsp;billion for 3 years) the Company expects strategic projects capital expenditures in 2023 to be higher than full year 2022 ($0.7 billion). Decarbonization capital expenditure spending is expected to accelerate
in full year 2023 versus the $0.2&nbsp;billion in full year 2022.<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">12</SUP> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Net cash used in other investing activities
in 3Q 2022 was $19&nbsp;million mainly related to investment in Form Energy Inc. (through the XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</SUP> innovation fund), as compared to $886&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 (primarily related to the
acquisition of the HBI plant, Texas). Net cash provided by other investing activities in 3Q 2021 of $1,184&nbsp;million included a cash inflow primarily related to the redemption of preferred shares of Cleveland Cliffs. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Net cash used in financing activities in 3Q 2022 was $219&nbsp;million as compared to $1,651&nbsp;million in 2Q 2022 and $2,740&nbsp;million in 3Q 2021. In 3Q 2022,
ArcelorMittal raised a <FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman">&#128;</FONT>600&nbsp;million 4 year note which was offset by the repurchase of 31&nbsp;million shares for a total value of $712&nbsp;million (of which $649&nbsp;million was paid by
the end of September 2022 and $63&nbsp;million settled in early October 2022) and paid dividends to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> shareholders of $124&nbsp;million mainly paid to
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> shareholders of AMMC. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Gross debt increased to $9.0&nbsp;billion as of September&nbsp;30, 2022, as compared
to $8.8&nbsp;billion as of June&nbsp;30, 2022, and $8.4&nbsp;billion as of December&nbsp;31, 2021. Net debt decreased by $0.3&nbsp;billion to $3.9&nbsp;billion as of September&nbsp;30, 2022, as compared to $4.2&nbsp;billion as of June&nbsp;30, 2022,
and decreased by $0.1&nbsp;billion from $4.0&nbsp;billion as of December&nbsp;31, 2021. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">As of September&nbsp;30, 2022, and June&nbsp;30, 2022, the Company had cash
and cash equivalents of $5.1&nbsp;billion and $4.6&nbsp;billion, respectively, and $5.5&nbsp;billion of available credit lines<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">7</SUP>. As of September&nbsp;30, 2022, the average debt maturity was 5.5
years. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Capital return </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Following the
completion of its previously announced share buyback plans (totaling 65.1&nbsp;million shares in 1H 2022), the Company announced a new share buyback program on July&nbsp;29, 2022 to purchase a further 60&nbsp;million shares by the end of May 2023.
This is the maximum shares purchasable under current shareholder authorization. Pursuant to this program, the Company repurchased ~31&nbsp;million shares at a cost of $0.7&nbsp;billion during the third quarter of 2022. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">Page 9 </P>

</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always">
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Outlook </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Company has adapted its capacity for 4Q 2022 to address the weak apparent demand environment and higher energy costs, particularly in Europe. Apparent demand
conditions are expected to improve once the current destocking phase reaches maturity. The Company is adapting its cost base during this period of low capacity utilization, optimizing energy consumption and reducing fixed costs of unproductive
capacity. At current spot levels, variable costs per tonne (raw materials and energy) are expected to decline in the 4Q 2022, but less than revenue per tonne. Working capital is believed to have peaked, and the unwind expected from 4Q 2022 and into
2023 is expected to support net cash provided by operating activities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Company expects to mitigate some of the fixed costs of idled capacity during 4Q 2022,
i.e., utilize economic unemployment support from governments; reduced working hours etc. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Based on the slowing real demand outlook and supply chain destocking,
ArcelorMittal expects the following demand by key region: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt">In the US, real consumption in 2022 is expected to grow, but a greater impact than previously expected from destocking
(particularly in the second half of the year) is forecast to lead to a slight contraction of apparent consumption by up to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-1%;</FONT> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt">In Europe, inflation headwinds are leading to slower (but still positive) real consumption growth in 2022, however the
impact of destocking is significant (particularly in the second half of the year) and expected to lead to a contraction of apparent consumption by up to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-7.0%;</FONT> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt">In Brazil, demand is in line with previous expectations, with a slight contraction in real consumption and a significant
reduction in inventory forecast (following destocking) to lead to a contraction in apparent consumption by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-10%</FONT> or more; </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt">In India, apparent consumption in 2022 is forecast to grow between +7.5% to +8.5%, which is at the upper end of our
previous expectations; </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:10pt">In the CIS region (which includes Commonwealth of Independent States and Ukraine), we forecast ASC to contract by up to <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-7.0%;</FONT> and </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

weak construction sector are forecast to lead to a decline in apparent demand of approximately <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">-3.5%.</FONT> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always">
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Appendix 5: Terms and definitions </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Unless indicated otherwise, or the context otherwise requires, references in this earnings release to the following terms have the meanings set out next to them below:
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Apparent steel consumption:</B> calculated as the sum of production plus imports minus exports. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Average steel selling prices:</B> calculated as steel sales divided by steel shipments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Cash and cash equivalents</B>: represents cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, and short-term investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Capital expenditures:</B> represents the purchase of property, plant and equipment and intangibles. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Crude steel production: </B>steel in the first solid state after melting, suitable for further processing or for sale. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Depreciation: </B>refers to amortization and depreciation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>EPS: </B>refers to
basic or diluted earnings per share. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Foreign exchange and other net financing income / (loss):</B> include foreign currency exchange impact, bank fees, interest
on pensions, impairment of financial assets, revaluation of derivative instruments and other charges that cannot be directly linked to operating results. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Gross
debt</B>: long-term debt and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">short-term</FONT> debt. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Iron ore reference prices:</B> refers to iron ore prices for 62% Fe CFR
China. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Kt:</B> refers to thousand metric tonnes. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>LTIF:</B> lost time injury
frequency rate equals lost time injuries per 1,000,000 worked hours, based on own personnel and contractors. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Mt: </B>refers to million metric tonnes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Net debt:</B> long-term debt and short-term debt less cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash and other restricted funds. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Net interest expense: </B>includes interest expense less interest income </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Operating results: </B>refers to operating income/(loss). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Operating segments:
</B>NAFTA segment includes the Flat, Long and Tubular operations of Canada, Mexico; and also includes all Mexico mines. The Brazil segment includes the Flat, Long and Tubular operations of Brazil and its neighboring countries including Argentina,
Costa Rica, Venezuela; and also includes Andrade and Serra Azul captive iron ore mines. The Europe segment includes the Flat, Long and Tubular operations of the European business, as well as Downstream Solutions, and also includes Bosnia and
Herzegovina captive iron ore mines. The ACIS segment includes the Flat, Long and Tubular operations of Kazakhstan, Ukraine and South Africa; and also includes the captive iron ore mines in Ukraine and iron ore and coal mines in Kazakhstan. Mining
segment includes iron ore operations of ArcelorMittal Mines Canada and ArcelorMittal Liberia. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Own iron ore production:</B> includes total of all finished
production of fines, concentrate, pellets and lumps and includes share of production. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Price-cost effect: </B>a lack of correlation or a lag in the corollary
relationship between raw material and steel prices, which can either have a positive (i.e., increased spread between steel prices and raw material costs) or negative effect (i.e., a squeeze or decreased spread between steel prices and raw material
costs). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Shipments:</B> information at segment and group level eliminates intra-segment shipments (which are primarily between Flat/Long plants and Tubular plants)
and inter-segment shipments respectively. Shipments of Downstream Solutions are excluded. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>STIP: </B>refers to short term incentive plan. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>LTIP: </B>refers to long term incentive plan. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Working capital change (working
capital investment / release): </B>Movement of change in working capital - trade accounts receivable plus inventories less trade and other accounts payable. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:96pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:11pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT
 COLOR="#ff0000"><B>Footnotes </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">1.</TD>

Standards (&#147;IFRS&#148;) as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (&#147;IASB&#148;). The interim financial information included in this announcement has also been prepared in accordance with IFRS applicable to interim periods,
however this announcement does not contain sufficient information to constitute an interim financial report as defined in International Accounting Standard 34, &#147;Interim Financial Reporting&#148;. The numbers in this press release have not been
audited. The </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

financial information and certain other information presented in a number of tables in this press release have been rounded to the nearest whole number or the nearest decimal. Therefore, the sum
of the numbers in a column may not conform exactly to the total figure given for that column. In addition, certain percentages presented in the tables in this press release reflect calculations based upon the underlying information prior to rounding
and, accordingly, may not conform exactly to the percentages that would be derived if the relevant calculations were based upon the rounded numbers. Segment information presented in this press release is prior to inter-segment eliminations and
certain adjustments made to operating result of the segments to reflect corporate costs, income from <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-steel</FONT> operations (e.g., logistics and shipping services) and the elimination of stock margins between
the segments. This press release also includes certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial/alternative performance measures. ArcelorMittal presents net debt and change in working capital as additional measures to enhance the
understanding of its financial position and provide additional information to investors and management with respect to the Company&#146;s cash flows, capital structure and its credit assessment. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT>
financial/alternative performance measures should be read in conjunction with, and not as an alternative for, ArcelorMittal&#146;s financial information prepared in accordance with IFRS. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">2.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">Effective 2Q 2021, ArcelorMittal retrospectively amended its presentation of reportable segments. The results of each mine
are accounted for within the steel segment that it primarily supplies. Summary of changes: NAFTA: all Mexico mines; Brazil: Andrade and Serra Azul mines; Europe: ArcelorMittal Prijedor mine (Bosnia and Herzegovina); ACIS: Kazakhstan and Ukraine
mines; and Mining: only AMMC and Liberia iron ore mines. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">3.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">LTIF figures presented for 3Q 2022 of 0.54x, 2Q 2022 of 0.67x, 3Q 2021 of 0.76x, 9M 2022 of 0.63x and 9M 2021 of 0.80x
exclude ArcelorMittal Italia (which was deconsolidated as from 2Q 2021 onwards). </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">4.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">AMNS India is debottlenecking its operations (steel shop and rolling parts) to achieve capacity of 8.6Mt per annum by the
end of 2024. AMNS India medium-term plans are to expand and grow initially to ~15Mt by early 2026 in Hazira (phase 1A) including automotive downstream and enhancements to iron ore operations, with estimated capital expenditures of ~$7.4&nbsp;billion
(for $0.8&nbsp;billion for debottlenecking, $1.0&nbsp;billion for downstream projects and $5.6&nbsp;billion for upstream projects. Phase 1A plans include a CRM2 complex and galvanizing and annealing line, 2 blast furnaces, steel shop, HSM, ancillary
equipment (including coke, sinter, networks, power, gas, oxygen plant etc.); and raw material handling. Start of BF2 expected in 2025 and BF3 in 2026. BF1 net capacity increase from 2Mtpa to 3Mtpa. There are further options to potentially grow to
20Mt per annum (Phase 1B). AMNS India has agreed to acquire port, power and other logistics and infrastructure assets in India from the Essar Group for a net value of ~$2.4bn. AMNS India has completed part of the power closing transaction on
October&nbsp;19, 2022 ($0.4 billion) whilst the remaining transaction closing is subject to the completion of certain corporate and regulatory approvals. In March 2021, AMNS India signed a Memorandum of Understanding (&#147;MoU&#148;) with the
Government of Odisha in view of building an integrated steel plant with a 12Mtpa capacity in Kendrapara district of state Odisha. A <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-feasibility</FONT> study report was submitted to the state government in 3Q
2021, and AMNS India is currently engaging with the government for further studies and clearances. Further options to build a 6Mtpa integrated steel plant are being assessed. The Thakurani mine is operating at full 5.5Mtpa capacity since 1Q 2021,
while the second Odisha pellet plant was commissioned and started in September 2021, adding 6Mtpa for a total 20Mtpa of pellet capacity. In addition, in September 2021, AMNS India commenced operations at Ghoraburhani - Sagasahi iron ore mine in
Odisha. The mine is set to gradually ramp up production to a rated capacity of 7.2Mtpa and contribute significantly to meeting AMNS India&#146;s long-term raw material requirements. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">5.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">AMNS Calvert (&#147;Calvert&#148;) has plans to construct a new 1.5Mt EAF and caster is expected to be completed in 2023.
The joint venture is to invest $775&nbsp;million. Option to add a further 1.5Mt EAF at lower capital expenditure intensity is being studied. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">7.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">On December&nbsp;19, 2018, ArcelorMittal signed a $5.5&nbsp;billion Revolving Credit Facility, with a five-year maturity
plus two <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> extension options. During the fourth quarter of 2019, ArcelorMittal executed the option to extend the facility to December&nbsp;19, 2024. The extension was completed for $5.4&nbsp;billion of
the available amount, with the remaining $0.1&nbsp;billion remaining with a maturity of December&nbsp;19, 2023. In December 2020, ArcelorMittal executed the second option to extend the facility, and the new maturity is now extended to
December&nbsp;19, 2025. On April&nbsp;30, 2021, ArcelorMittal amended its $5.5&nbsp;billion RCF to align with its sustainability and climate action strategy. As of September&nbsp;30, 2022, the $5.5&nbsp;billion revolving credit facility was fully
available. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">8.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> is designed to bring together all of ArcelorMittal&#146;s
reduced, low and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">zero-carbon</FONT> products and steelmaking activities, as well as wider initiatives and green innovation projects, into a single effort focused on achieving demonstrable progress towards carbon
neutral steel. Alongside the new XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> brand, we have launched three XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> initiatives: the XCarb<SUP
STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> innovation fund, XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> green steel certificates and XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> recycled and
renewably produced for products made via the Electric Arc Furnace route using scrap. The Company is offering green steel using a system of certificates (XCarb<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&reg;</SUP> green certificates). These will
be issued by an independent auditor to certify tonnes of CO2 savings achieved through the Company&#146;s investment in decarbonization technologies in Europe. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Net-zero</FONT> equivalence is determined by assigning
CO2 savings certificates equivalent to CO2 per tonne of steel produced in 2018 as the reference. The certificates will relate to the tonnes of CO2 saved in total, as a direct result of the decarbonization projects being implemented across a number
of its European sites. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">9.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">In addition to the AMNS India and Calvert joint ventures, the Company has important investments in China that provide
valuable dividend streams and growth optionality. VAMA, our 50:50 joint venture with Hunan Valin, is a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">state-of-the-art</FONT></FONT></FONT> facility
focused on rolling steel for high-demanding applications in particular automotive. The business is performing well and plans to expand the current capacity by 40% to 2Mtpa over the next 2 years, financed from its own resources. The investment will
allow VAMA to broaden its product portfolio and further enhance its competitiveness. This will in turn enable VAMA to meet the growing demand of high value add solutions from the Chinese automotive / new energy vehicle (NEV) market and propel it to
be among the top automotive steel players in China by 2025. ArcelorMittal also owns a 37% interest in China Oriental, one of the largest <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">H-Beam</FONT> producers in China which has recently upgraded its asset
portfolio and benefits from a strong balance sheet position. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

and $885&nbsp;million as of September&nbsp;30, 2022, June&nbsp;30, 2022, and December&nbsp;31, 2021, respectively. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

levels of pig iron production). Iron ore production was temporarily suspended in 3Q 2022 (from ~55% capacity run rate in 2Q 2022). Iron ore production in Ukraine has restarted in early October 2022 at ~25% level. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">14.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">On March&nbsp;30, 2022 Votorantim exercised the put option right it has under its shareholders&#146; agreement with the
Company to sell its entire equity interest in ArcelorMittal Brasil to the Company, following the acquisition of Votorantim S.A.&#146;s long steel business in Brazil in 2018, which became a wholly-owned subsidiary of ArcelorMittal Brasil. The
exercise price is calculated pursuant to an agreed formula in the shareholders&#146; agreement which applies a 6x multiple of ArcelorMittal Brasil Longs Business EBITDA in the four immediately preceding calendar quarters from the date of the put
option exercise (subject to certain adjustments, such as the exclusion of any unusual, infrequent or abnormal events) less an assumed net debt of BRL 6.2&nbsp;billion times 15%. ArcelorMittal Brasil calculated the put option exercise price in the
amount of $0.2&nbsp;billion. Votorantim S.A. has indicated that it does not agree with ArcelorMittal Brasil&#146;s calculation of the exercise price and filed a request for arbitration on September&nbsp;28, 2022. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">Following a favorable and unappealable decision issued in May 2022 with respect to taxpayers&#146; right to register the
Pis/Cofins credits over scrap purchases, ArcelorMittal Brasil recorded a gain in the amount of $0.2&nbsp;billion for the previous periods. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">16.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">The Company has introduced a 50% increase in the short term incentive plan (STIP) link to safety performance (with
fatalities acting as a circuit breaker); increased the safety target in STIP to 15% and long term incentive plan (LTIP) to 10%; and included ESG objectives in LTIP. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">17.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">On October&nbsp;13, 2022, ArcelorMittal together with the governments of Canada and Ontario, broke ground on its
CAD$1.8&nbsp;billion investment decarbonization project at the ArcelorMittal Dofasco plant in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. The governments of Canada and Ontario having committed CAD$400&nbsp;million and CAD$500&nbsp;million respectively to the overall
project cost. The project will fundamentally change the way steel is made at ArcelorMittal Dofasco, transitioning the site to direct reduced iron-electric arc furnace steelmaking, which carries a considerably lower carbon footprint and removes coal
from the ironmaking process. The new 2.5Mt capacity DRI furnace will initially operate on natural gas but will be constructed &#145;hydrogen ready&#146; so it can transition to green hydrogen when a sufficient and cost-effective supply becomes
available. The first onsite construction work will begin in January 2023. Construction on the new assets is currently expected to be completed in 2026, at which point a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-18</FONT> month transition phase will begin
with both steelmaking streams <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(BF-BOF</FONT> and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">DRI-EAF)</FONT> active. The transition is expected to be completed by 2028. In addition to the new DRI facility, the project also
involves the construction of an EAF capable of producing 2.4&nbsp;million tonnes of high-quality steel through ArcelorMittal Dofasco&#146;s existing casting, rolling and finishing facilities. Modification of ArcelorMittal Dofasco&#146;s existing EAF
facility and continuous casters will also be undertaken to align productivity, quality and energy capabilities between all assets in the new footprint. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">18.</TD>

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">19.</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="left">In early November 2022, ArcelorMittal announced that it is preparing to reduce its activity at the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Fos-sur-Mer</FONT></FONT> site due to the slowdown in steel demand and the impact of energy prices. The Company expects a temporary shutdown of one of the site&#146;s two blast furnaces as
of December 2022. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="right">Exhibit 99.3 </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><U>Third Quarter Results </U></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On November&nbsp;10, 2022,
ArcelorMittal announced its results for the three month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2022. See Exhibit&nbsp;99.2 hereto. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><U>Other Recent
Developments </U></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Legal Proceedings Update </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In 2013, ArcelorMittal Brasil received a tax assessment in relation to the 2008-2010 tax years for IRPJ and CSL in relation to (i)&nbsp;the amortization of
goodwill on the acquisition of Mendes J&uacute;nior Siderurgia, Dedini Siderurgia and CST, (ii)&nbsp;the 341 Consolidated financial statements amortization of goodwill arising from the MTO made by ArcelorMittal
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(ex-Mittal</FONT> Steel N.V.) to minority shareholders of Arcelor Brasil in connection with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">two-step</FONT> merger of Arcelor and Mittal Steel N.V. and (iii)&nbsp;CSL and IRPJ
over profits of controlled companies in Argentina, Costa Rica, Venezuela and the Netherlands. The amount claimed totals $375&nbsp;million. In October 2014, the administrative tribunal of the first instance found in favor of the Federal Revenue
Service and ArcelorMittal Brasil filed its appeal in November 2014. In September 2017, the administrative tribunal of the second instance found in favor of the Federal Revenue Service. ArcelorMittal Brasil filed a motion for clarification with
respect to this decision, which was denied, and thereafter filed an appeal to the administrative tribunal of the third instance. In November 2022, the third instance of the administrative court found in favor ArcelorMittal Brasil in relation to the
claim regarding the goodwill amortization ($322 million). The claim related to the taxation of controlled foreign companies&#146; profits ($53 million) was postponed. </P>
